| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

`o365_management_activity`

New GreatXML Exploit Bypasses Windows BitLocker via Recovery Partition XML Files

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 9 use cases 4 techniques 7 kill-chain phases detected

Security researcher Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse and MSNightmare) has released a new Windows BitLocker bypass dubbed GreatXML, a day after they published an exploit for Microsoft Defender. "This was an accidental discovery, it took a total of 4 hours to find this," the researcher said in a post on Blogger. "If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you're

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Windows Defender Offline scan trigger — GreatXML vulnerability precondition · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] GreatXML BitLocker Bypass — unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml dropped on recovery partition
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] User-initiated reboot to Windows Recovery Environment (GreatXML trigger) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
GreatXML BitLocker Bypass — unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml dropped on recovery partition AIWeaponization High
Detects file writes of the two specific XML artefacts the GreatXML PoC requires: an `unattend.xml` at the root of a non-system volume (the recovery partition) and/or a `ReAgent.xml` under a `\Recovery\WindowsRE\` path on a volume other than the OS install. The legitimate ReAgent.xml lives in `C:\Windows\System32\Recovery\`; writes elsewhere are the exploit staging the WinRE boot. Rationale: Anchors on the two exact filenames the article names (`unattend.xml`, `Recovery/WindowsRE/ReAgent.xml`) and carves out their legitimate Windows locations (`C:\Windows\System32\Recovery\` for ReAgent, `C:\Windows\Panther\`/`Sysprep\` for unattend). A write outside those canonical paths plus excluding TrustedInstaller/Defender/reagentc as initiator yields very high fidelity because no normal Windows component writes these names to a recovery-partition path.
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MDT/SCCM task-sequence staging an OS image and dropping unattend.xml to a custom path on a USB/PXE volume
  • OEM imaging tools (Dell Image Assist, Lenovo Smart Standby) writing OEM recovery configuration
  • IT admin manually customising WinRE via `reagentc /setreimage` workflow which can copy ReAgent.xml
  • Backup software (Veeam, Macrium) restoring system-state including recovery partition contents
  • Researcher / penetration-tester intentionally reproducing the GreatXML PoC on a test host
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Microsoft Deployment Toolkit\", @"\SMSTSWiz\", @"\osdcloud\") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("DISM.exe","setup.exe","OSDSetupHook.exe","TSManager.exe","smsts.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the InitiatingProcess tree and the user account. Confirm whether the host has an active deployment / imaging task running (check SCCM/MDT logs) or whether the initiating process is a known imaging tool. Note whether the recovery partition was just mounted (look for nearby `diskpart`, `mountvol`, or `assign letter=` activity). Step 2 — Contain: if no legitimate imaging context, isolate the host via MDE Live Response and block the user from initiating a reboot. Preserve the recovery partition contents — copy the two XML files for IR. Do NOT let the host reboot until reviewed; a Shift+Restart finishes the exploit. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the same user/host for prior `MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot` or `Start-MpWDOScan` (the prerequisite), nearby `reagentc.exe /boottore` or `shutdown.exe /r /o` (the trigger), and look across the fleet for other hosts that received the same two file names from the same source process or share / IP.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (FileName =~ "ReAgent.xml"
            and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\Recovery"
            and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Recovery"
            and FolderPath has @"\Recovery\WindowsRE")
     or (FileName =~ "unattend.xml"
            and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\"
            and FolderPath !contains @"\Panther\"
            and FolderPath !contains @"\Sysprep\")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","reagentc.exe","wuauclt.exe","TiWorker.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated" or EventType =~ "FileModified" or EventType =~ "FileRenamed"
| where (TargetFileName =~ "ReAgent.xml"
            and TargetFilePath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\Recovery"
            and TargetFilePath !startswith @"C:\Recovery"
            and TargetFilePath has @"\Recovery\WindowsRE")
     or (TargetFileName =~ "unattend.xml"
            and TargetFilePath !startswith @"C:\Windows\"
            and TargetFilePath !contains @"\Panther\"
            and TargetFilePath !contains @"\Sysprep\")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","reagentc.exe","wuauclt.exe","TiWorker.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, EventType,
          ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GreatXML BitLocker Bypass - Recovery Partition XML Drop
id: 7a1e3f8c-b9d2-4a51-9e6f-2c4b8d9a1e30
description: Detects creation of unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml outside their canonical Windows paths - the staging step of the GreatXML BitLocker bypass that drops these files onto the recovery partition before a WinRE boot.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1542.005
  - attack.t1112
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  reagent_xml:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml'
  reagent_xml_filter:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - 'C:\Windows\System32\Recovery\'
      - 'C:\Recovery\'
  unattend_xml:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\unattend.xml'
  unattend_xml_filter:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - 'C:\Windows\'
      - '\Panther\'
      - '\Sysprep\'
  benign_writer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\MpCmdRun.exe'
      - '\reagentc.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
  condition: ((reagent_xml and not reagent_xml_filter) or (unattend_xml and not unattend_xml_filter)) and not benign_writer
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\Recovery\\WindowsRE\\ReAgent.xml OR *\\recovery\\windowsre\\reagent.xml) OR (@TargetFilename:(*\\unattend.xml OR *\\Unattend.xml OR *\\UNATTEND.XML) AND -@TargetFilename:(*\\Windows\\* OR *\\Panther\\* OR *\\Sysprep\\*))) AND -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\MsMpEng.exe OR *\\MpCmdRun.exe OR *\\reagentc.exe OR *\\TiWorker.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| (regex("(?i)\\\\Recovery\\\\WindowsRE\\\\ReAgent\\.xml$", field=TargetFileName) AND NOT regex("(?i)^C:\\\\(Windows\\\\System32\\\\Recovery|Recovery)\\\\", field=TargetFileName)) OR (regex("(?i)\\\\unattend\\.xml$", field=TargetFileName) AND NOT regex("(?i)\\\\(Windows|Panther|Sysprep)\\\\", field=TargetFileName))
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|MsMpEng|MpCmdRun|reagentc|TiWorker)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.process_id) as process_id values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Windows\\System32\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Recovery\\*") AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\WindowsRE\\*") OR (Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Windows\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Panther\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Sysprep\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_name,"(?i)(TrustedInstaller|MsMpEng|MpCmdRun|reagentc|TiWorker)\.exe$")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.process_id) as process_id values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Windows\\System32\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Recovery\\*") AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\WindowsRE\\*") OR (Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Windows\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Panther\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Sysprep\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_name,"(?i)(TrustedInstaller|MsMpEng|MpCmdRun|reagentc|TiWorker)\.exe$")
User-initiated reboot to Windows Recovery Environment (GreatXML trigger) AIExploitation Medium
Detects the WinRE-boot trigger the GreatXML PoC requires: either `reagentc.exe /boottore` programmatically, or `shutdown.exe /r /o` (the CLI equivalent of Shift+Restart). Pair with UC1 (recovery-partition XML drop) on the same host to confirm the bypass attempt. Rationale: `reagentc.exe /boottore` and `shutdown.exe /r /o` are the only two CLI paths to a WinRE boot; both are uncommon outside of IT-helpdesk troubleshooting and OS upgrade flows. Pairs with UC1 - a recovery-partition XML drop followed within minutes by a WinRE-boot trigger from the same host is the full GreatXML chain.
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Helpdesk technician walking a user through Advanced Startup to repair boot issues
  • Windows Update / feature update flows occasionally invoke `reagentc` during servicing
  • SCCM / Intune remediation scripts that schedule a reboot to recovery for repair
  • Power user troubleshooting their own machine via Settings -> Recovery -> Restart now
  • Hardware vendor diagnostics tools (Dell SupportAssist, Lenovo Vantage) booting to recovery
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","UsoClient.exe","SupportAssistAgent.exe","VantageService.exe") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "services.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the parent-process chain for the reboot command. Helpdesk-driven recovery boots usually come from `explorer.exe` or `mmc.exe` via Settings; scripted attacker chains often come from `cmd.exe`/`powershell.exe` or an SSH/RDP session. Cross-check whether the user has an open helpdesk ticket. Step 2 — Contain: if the host has UC1 (recovery-partition XML write) inside the prior 60 minutes, treat as confirmed GreatXML chain - block the reboot through your EDR/MDM rebooting policy and isolate the host before WinRE is reached. Step 3 — Hunt: search for `MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot` or `Start-MpWDOScan` on the same host in the prior 30 days (the precondition) and pivot the user identity across other endpoints for the same chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "reagentc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/boottore","-boottore","boottore"))
     or (FileName =~ "shutdown.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/o" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/r","/g"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\reagentc.exe" and (CommandLine has_any ("/boottore","-boottore","boottore")))
     or (NewProcessName endswith @"\shutdown.exe" and CommandLine has "/o" and CommandLine has_any ("/r","/g"))
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Reboot to Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) - GreatXML Trigger
id: 8b2f4a9d-c0e3-4b62-af70-3d5c9e0b2f41
description: Detects the CLI invocations that boot a Windows host into WinRE - the trigger step of the GreatXML BitLocker bypass after unattend.xml and ReAgent.xml have been staged on the recovery partition.
references:

logsource:
  category: process_creation

detection:
  reagentc:
    Image|endswith: '\reagentc.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/boottore'
      - '-boottore'
      - 'boottore'
  shutdown_to_recovery:
    Image|endswith: '\shutdown.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/o'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/o'
  shutdown_reboot_flag:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/r'
      - '/g'
  condition: reagentc or (shutdown_to_recovery and shutdown_reboot_flag)
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\\reagentc.exe OR *\\ReAgentC.exe OR *\\REAGENTC.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*boottore* OR *BootToRE* OR *BOOTTORE*)) OR (@Image:(*\\shutdown.exe OR *\\Shutdown.exe OR *\\SHUTDOWN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*\/o* OR *-o*) AND @CommandLine:(*\/r* OR *\/g*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\reagentc\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/boottore/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\shutdown\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\s\/o\b/i AND CommandLine=/\s\/(r|g)\b/i)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process_cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" AND (Processes.process="*boottore*" OR Processes.process="*BootToRE*")) OR (Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" AND Processes.process="*/o*" AND (Processes.process="*/r*" OR Processes.process="*/g*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process_cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" AND (Processes.process="*boottore*" OR Processes.process="*BootToRE*")) OR (Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" AND Processes.process="*/o*" AND (Processes.process="*/r*" OR Processes.process="*/g*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$")
Windows Defender Offline scan trigger — GreatXML vulnerability precondition AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts for hosts that initiated a Windows Defender Offline scan via `MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot` or PowerShell `Start-MpWDOScan`. Per the article, this action puts the host into the state that makes the GreatXML bypass exploitable; surfacing it gives an audit of which endpoints are now susceptible to recovery-partition XML staging. Rationale: Article quote: 'If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you're automatically vulnerable to a BitLocker bypass.' The two canonical ways to invoke WDO are `MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot` and the `Start-MpWDOScan` PowerShell cmdlet - both are uncommon in fleet baselines and worth tracking as an exposure-audit hunt rather than an alert.
ATT&CKT1518.001 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Helpdesk running WDO scan to remediate a stubborn malware detection
  • User-initiated WDO scan via Windows Security UI as part of a deep-scan workflow
  • Endpoint-management policy that schedules periodic WDO scans
  • IR analyst running WDO as part of incident triage on a suspected-compromised host
  • Vendor-driven malware-cleanup recommendations that suggest running WDO
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("svchost.exe","MsMpEng.exe","SenseIR.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "services.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm whether the WDO invocation aligns with a known IT-driven scan ticket or user-initiated UI action. The parent process tells you - `services.exe` -> scheduled task, `explorer.exe` -> user UI, scripted parents are unusual. Step 2 — Audit: flag the host as 'GreatXML-vulnerable' in your asset inventory and prioritise it for the next patch cycle / WinRE reset (`reagentc /disable` then `/enable`). Until then, monitor for UC1 + UC2 chain on that host. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot the user across other endpoints for similar WDO invocations and look for clusters that suggest an attacker priming many hosts at once.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-WDOBoot","WDOBoot"))
     or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Invocations = count(),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine),
            Parents = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 8)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName
| order by LastSeen desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\MpCmdRun.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("-WDOBoot","WDOBoot"))
     or (NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" and CommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
     or (NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe" and CommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Invocations = count(),
            SampleCmd = any(CommandLine)
            by Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName
| order by LastSeen desc

description: Surfaces hosts that have initiated a Windows Defender Offline scan via MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot or PowerShell Start-MpWDOScan. The article notes that any host which has run WDO is automatically susceptible to the GreatXML BitLocker bypass.

| (ImageFileName=/\\MpCmdRun\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/WDOBoot/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/Start-MpWDOScan/i)

ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process_cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="MpCmdRun.exe" AND Processes.process="*WDOBoot*") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND Processes.process="*Start-MpWDOScan*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$")

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.

Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,

AuditLogs

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:

CodeIgniter4 ext_in bypass: HTTP POST upload to PHP/PHAR filename on upload endpoint AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the CVE-2026-48062 exploit attempt at the wire — POSTs to CodeIgniter4-style upload endpoints (avatar/profile/upload handlers) whose multipart filename uses a PHP-executable extension. Catches polyglot upload attempts before the file lands on disk. Rationale: Article names the exact vulnerable rule combo `mime_in[avatar,image/gif]|ext_in[avatar,gif]` and the canonical exploit filename `shell.php` — this hunt catches the POST containing that filename pattern on upload-shaped endpoints. Article also calls out `$file->move($path)` preserving the original filename, so the .php in the URI survives to disk. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1036.008
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PHP application endpoints that genuinely accept POSTs to .php handlers (e.g. action=upload.php in form)
  • Authenticated CMS administrators uploading PHP plugins/themes via admin UI
  • Bug-bounty researchers or internal pentest activity targeting upload forms
  • WordPress/Drupal core update mechanisms POSTing to admin-ajax.php
  • Composer/package-manager dependency callbacks hitting framework upload utilities
Suppression filter
| where not (csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/(wp-admin|administrator|admin-ajax\.php|drupal/admin)") | where not (csUserAgent has_any ("WordPress","Drupal","Joomla","composer"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull full request body for the matched POST (need WAF or full-PCAP for body). Confirm the multipart `filename=` parameter contains `.php`/`.phar` AND the Content-Type header is `image/*`. Check if the destination path is under a web-accessible directory (not `writable/uploads`). 2) Contain — if confirmed, quarantine the dropped file by hash, block the source IP at WAF/CDN, and rotate any credentials the webserver process has access to (DB creds in .env, S3 IAM keys). 3) Hunt — pivot to UC `Webserver writes PHP/PHAR to upload directory` on the same host and time window; check for outbound connections from php-fpm/w3wp in the next 60 minutes; scan webroot for any .php files modified post-upload.
// CodeIgniter4 ext_in bypass attempt — POST to upload-style endpoint with .php-ish filename in URI
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/(upload|avatar|profile|image|file)"
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|pht)(/|$)" or csUriQuery matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)"
| where toint(scStatus) between (200 .. 399)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus, csBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: CodeIgniter4 ext_in Bypass - Upload POST with PHP Filename
id: 7a3d2c1e-4f8b-4a91-bc62-3e2a9c1f8d44
description: HTTP POST to a CodeIgniter4-style upload endpoint where the filename in the URI carries a PHP-executable extension (.php/.phar/.phtml). Maps to CVE-2026-48062 ext_in validation bypass where mime_in[image/gif]+ext_in[gif] passes but the saved filename is shell.php.

Webserver process writes PHP/PHAR file to web-accessible upload directory AIInstallation High
Detects the post-bypass landing — php-fpm, w3wp, nginx, httpd or php-cgi creating a .php/.phar/.phtml/.phps file under common CodeIgniter4 upload paths (uploads/, avatars/, public/, writable/). This is the moment the polyglot exploit succeeds and a webshell hits disk. Rationale: Article explicitly describes the impact path: `save uploaded files using the original client filename: $file->move($path)` + `store uploads in a web-accessible directory` + `allow PHP or other executable files to run from that directory`. Detecting the webserver process itself writing a .php family file under those exact paths is the highest-fidelity post-exploit signal — a webserver writing executable script content to its own document root is the textbook webshell-drop pattern (T1505.003). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190 T1036.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress / Drupal / Joomla plugin or theme installations writing PHP files under wp-content/uploads or sites/default/files
  • Composer dependency installs under vendor/ (excluded by path filter)
  • CMS in-place upgrade processes downloading PHP files via core updater
  • Cache-warming or compile-on-write frameworks (e.g. Smarty/Twig writing pre-compiled .php caches under public/)
  • Application deployments via CI/CD that copy PHP files to public webroot
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any (@"\wp-content\plugins\", @"\wp-content\upgrade\", @"\sites\default\files\php\", @"\vendor\", @"\cache\")) | where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer","wp-cli","drush","artisan"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the file (SHA256 from the event), inspect first 32 bytes for a GIF magic header (47 49 46 38) followed by `<?php` or PHP shell signatures (`eval(`, `base64_decode(`, `system(`, `assert(`). Check FileSize — webshells are typically <20KB. Pull the InitiatingProcessAccountName and confirm it's the webserver service account (www-data, IUSR, apppool identity). 2) Contain — quarantine the file (move out of webroot or `chmod 000`), block remote IPs that POSTed to that path in the prior 15 min at the WAF/CDN, and revoke webserver-context credentials (.env DB creds, S3/IAM session tokens). Take a memory image of the webserver process before killing. 3) Hunt — pivot to `DeviceProcessEvents` for the same `DeviceName`/`InitiatingProcessAccountName` to find php-fpm/w3wp spawning shells; check `DeviceNetworkEvents` for outbound from the webserver to non-standard destinations; scan the entire webroot for other .php files modified in the prior 24h by the same process; audit CodeIgnite
// CVE-2026-48062 CodeIgniter4 ext_in bypass — webserver drops PHP under public upload path
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","apache2","caddy.exe","caddy")
| extend Ext = tolower(extract(@"\.([^\.\\/]+)$", 1, FileName))
| where Ext in ("php","phar","phtml","phps","pht","phtm")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\uploads\", @"/uploads/", @"\avatars\", @"/avatars/", @"\public\", @"/public/", @"\writable\", @"/writable/", @"\public_html\", @"/public_html/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48062 — PHP/PHAR landed in web-accessible upload directory by webserver process
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","apache2","caddy")
| where tolower(TargetFileExtension) in ("php","phar","phtml","phps","pht")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\uploads\", @"/uploads/", @"\avatars\", @"/avatars/", @"\public\", @"/public/", @"\writable\", @"/writable/", @"\public_html\", @"/public_html/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileSize
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Webserver Process Drops PHP File in Public Upload Directory
id: c4e9a8b1-2d7f-4a35-9e1c-6b4f8d2a9e07
description: CodeIgniter4 ext_in upload-validation bypass (CVE-2026-48062) results in a polyglot file (e.g. shell.php containing GIF bytes) being saved via $file->move($path) under a web-accessible directory. This rule fires when the PHP-FPM / IIS worker / nginx / Apache process writes a .php-family file beneath uploads/, avatars/, public/, or writable/.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
  - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html

    Image|endswith:
      - '\php-fpm.exe'

falsepositives:
  - CMS plugin/theme installs by administrators (WordPress/Drupal/Joomla)
  - Composer dependency installs under vendor/ (different path)
level: high

| ContextImageFileName=/(php-fpm|w3wp|httpd|nginx|php-cgi|php|apache2|caddy)(\.exe)?$/i

HTTP GET access to PHP file under CodeIgniter4 writable/upload directory AIExploitation High
Catches the webshell-trigger phase — an HTTP client requesting a .php/.phar file under the same writable upload directory CodeIgniter4 stores user-controlled uploads to. Combined with the upload UCs, this temporally correlates with the polyglot drop and proves code execution attempt. Rationale: Article workarounds explicitly recommend `Save uploads outside the public web root, preferably under writable/uploads` — so any HTTP request that successfully resolves a .php file under those exact paths means the configuration is vulnerable AND someone is executing the dropped payload. Path strings (`writable/uploads`, `avatars`) are quoted directly from the GHSA body. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sites that legitimately serve PHP from /uploads (rare; typically a config mistake worth investigating regardless)
  • Search-engine crawlers indexing pre-existing public PHP endpoints under those paths
  • Internal pentest / DAST scans against the upload directory
  • Legacy application that drops PHP under writable/ intentionally (e.g. custom theme installer)
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys, Burp) probing upload directories
Suppression filter
| where not (csUserAgent has_any ("Googlebot","bingbot","DuckDuckBot","YandexBot","AhrefsBot")) | where not (cIP in ("<scanner-ip-1>","<scanner-ip-2>"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full URI and any query string for the request; check the response status (2xx = code executed; 403/404 = blocked or missing). Cross-reference the requested filename against UC `Webserver writes PHP/PHAR to upload directory` from the prior 60 minutes — if it matches, you have a confirmed chain: drop → trigger. 2) Contain — block the source IP at the edge, remove the .php file from the upload directory (or make the directory non-executable via `php_admin_flag engine off` / Apache `<FilesMatch \.ph(p|ar|tml)$>Deny from all</FilesMatch>` / nginx `location ~ ^/uploads/.*\.php$ { return 403; }`), and force-restart php-fpm to drop in-memory webshell state. 3) Hunt — pivot to outbound `DeviceNetworkEvents`/`NetworkConnectIP4` from the webserver host in the response time window for C2 connections; review `DeviceProcessEvents` for php-fpm/w3wp spawning child processes; scan `DeviceFileEvents` for any other recent .php writes under public paths.
// HTTP access to .php under CodeIgniter4 writable/upload directory — webshell trigger
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csMethod in ("GET","POST")
| where csUriStem matches regex @"(?i)/(writable/uploads|public/uploads|uploads/avatars|avatars|public/avatars|uploads)/.+\.(php|phar|phtml|phps|pht)(/|$)"
| where toint(scStatus) < 500
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count(), AnyUA=any(csUserAgent), AnyStatus=any(scStatus) by Computer, cIP, csUriStem
| where Hits >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc

(source:nginx.access OR source:apache.access OR source:iis) @http.method:(GET OR POST) @http.url_details.path:(*/writable/uploads/* OR */public/uploads/* OR */uploads/avatars/* OR */avatars/*) @http.url_details.path:(*.php* OR *.PHP* OR *.phar* OR *.phtml*) @http.status_code:[100 TO 499]

| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web where (Web.http_method=GET OR Web.http_method=POST) AND (Web.url="*/writable/uploads/*" OR Web.url="*/public/uploads/*" OR Web.url="*/uploads/avatars/*" OR Web.url="*/avatars/*" OR Web.url="*/public/avatars/*") AND (Web.url="*.php*" OR Web.url="*.phar*" OR Web.url="*.phtml*" OR Web.url="*.phps*") AND Web.status<500 by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.http_method Web.http_user_agent Web.status _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | sort - _time

PHP webserver process (php-fpm / w3wp / nginx) spawns shell or LOLBin AIActions on Objectives High
Detects post-exploitation hands-on activity after the CVE-2026-48062 webshell lands — PHP-FPM, IIS app-pool worker, or Apache spawning cmd/powershell/bash/certutil/curl. This is the highest-confidence signal that the dropped polyglot was executed and an operator is now interacting via the webshell. Rationale: Article confirms the attack outcome: `In those conditions, this may lead to arbitrary code execution`. A webserver process — which under normal application flow should never need cmd.exe, bash, certutil, or netcat — spawning one of those is the classical webshell post-exploit signature (T1505.003). Parent-process list is grounded in the PHP runtime stack the advisory targets (php-fpm via Apache/nginx, w3wp on IIS, php-cgi). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.001 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • PHP applications invoking shell_exec/exec/system for legitimate media processing (imagemagick `convert`, `ffmpeg`, `exiftool`, `gs`)
  • CMS backup plugins (UpdraftPlus, Duplicator) shelling out to tar/zip via PHP
  • Composer running `php artisan`, `wp-cli`, or `drush` as a child of PHP-FPM during maintenance windows
  • CI/CD-triggered deployment scripts on the webserver host (rsync, git pull)
  • Monitoring agents probing webserver health via PHP scripts that call uname/whoami
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("convert -","ffmpeg -i","exiftool ","identify -","magick ","gs -","pdftotext ")) | where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("artisan","wp-cli","drush","composer"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full `ProcessCommandLine` and parent `InitiatingProcessCommandLine`. Recon commands (`whoami`, `id`, `uname -a`, `cat /etc/passwd`) confirm hands-on. Cross-check the parent php-fpm/w3wp process for any recent .php file under uploads/ that it executed in the prior hour. 2) Contain — kill the spawned child PID, isolate the host from the network (Defender `Isolate machine`, AWS SG quarantine), preserve memory of the PHP worker for forensics, restart php-fpm/IIS app pool to drop in-memory webshell state, and force-rotate any credentials accessible from the webserver host (DB creds, IAM, .env secrets). 3) Hunt — pivot to `DeviceNetworkEvents`/`NetworkConnectIP4` from the same PID for outbound C2; check `DeviceFileEvents` for additional .php drops by the same `InitiatingProcessId`; review `DeviceLogonEvents` for lateral movement attempts from the host; audit other internal CodeIgniter4 apps for the same version <4.7.3.
// CVE-2026-48062 post-exploit — PHP webserver spawns shell / LOLBin / network tool
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","apache2","caddy.exe","caddy")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","ash","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget","wget.exe","nc.exe","ncat.exe","python.exe","python","python3","perl.exe","perl","ruby.exe","ruby","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","socat","whoami.exe","id","uname")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
// Webserver process spawns shell/LOLBin post-upload — Sentinel SecurityEvent 4688 path
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentBase = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1])), ChildBase = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ParentBase in ("php-fpm.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","caddy.exe")
| where ChildBase in ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","nc.exe","ncat.exe","python.exe","perl.exe","ruby.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","whoami.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
| union (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","w3wp.exe","httpd","nginx","php-cgi","php.exe","apache2","caddy")
    | where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell","pwsh","bash","sh","certutil","bitsadmin","curl","wget","ncat","nc","python","perl","ruby","wscript","cscript","mshta","whoami")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, SubjectUserName = ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName = TargetProcessName, CommandLine = TargetProcessCommandLine, TokenElevationType = ActingProcessIntegrityLevel
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'

      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
