Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FortiGate SSL-VPN / admin credential brute-force or spray from single source · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] First successful FortiGate admin/SSL-VPN login from never-seen ASN after failure burst · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Machine-cadence post-auth FortiGate CLI/API calls in single session (MCP-orchestrated)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound JSON-RPC or LLM-API egress from network appliance / edge device · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
FortiGate SSL-VPN / admin credential brute-force or spray from single source AIDelivery Medium
Detects the high-volume failed-then-successful FortiGate admin or SSL-VPN logins characteristic of the Feb 2026 MCP-orchestrated campaign in which an autonomous agent sprayed weak credentials against 2,516 queued appliances. Looks for one source IP touching many usernames or many devices with one or two attempts each, followed by a single success. Rationale: Article says actor 'queued 2,516 devices across 106 countries' with 'no zero-days needed, just weak credentials' via a custom MCP server. The detection grounds on multi-target single-source spray cadence specifically against FortiGate SSL-VPN/admin auth, not generic brute-force.
ATT&CKT1110.001 T1110.003 T1110.004
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Misconfigured customer VPN client retrying with cached bad password after policy change
  • Authorized BAS / red-team credential-spray runs against the same edge appliance
  • External vulnerability scanner (Qualys, Tenable) doing auth-checks against the SSL-VPN portal
  • NAT egress from a partner network where many users share one source IP and several fail MFA simultaneously
  • Mobile-device password change causing burst of 401s from a fleet of corporate phones
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<bas_egress_ip_1>", "<bas_egress_ip_2>"])) | where SourceUserName !startswith "redteam-"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the source IP is on the approved BAS/red-team allow-list and whether any of the targeted usernames exist on the appliance; pull the actual admin/sslvpn log lines for the success event. 2) Contain: if not authorized, immediately disable the affected admin account, expire all SSL-VPN sessions for that user, block the source IP at the edge ACL, and force password reset + MFA enrollment. 3) Hunt: pivot on the source IP and ASN across all edge devices in the last 14 days; check for outbound connections from the FortiGate management plane to LLM/MCP endpoints; review config-change logs for the success window.
let WindowMin = 10m;
let FailedThreshold = 10;
let Failures = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 8443) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd", "fgfm")
    | summarize Failed = count(), Users = make_set(InitiatingProcessAccountName), Devices = make_set(DeviceName) by RemoteIP, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
    | where Failed >= FailedThreshold;
Failures
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMin = 10m;
let FailedThreshold = 10;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where Activity has_any ("login", "ssl-vpn", "admin") or Message has_any ("login failed", "authentication failed", "ssl-vpn-login")
| extend Outcome = case(DeviceAction has "fail" or Message has_any ("failed", "denied"), "failure", DeviceAction has "success" or Message has "login success", "success", "unknown")
| summarize Failed = countif(Outcome == "failure"), Succeeded = countif(Outcome == "success"), Users = make_set(SourceUserName, 50), Hosts = make_set(DeviceExternalID, 50) by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where Failed >= FailedThreshold and Succeeded >= 1
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) (@source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) OR @network.client.port:(443 OR 10443)) (@evt.outcome:failure OR @msg:("login failed" OR "authentication failed" OR ssl-vpn-login)) -@network.client.ip:10.0.0.0/8

First successful FortiGate admin/SSL-VPN login from never-seen ASN after failure burst AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the post-spray foothold step from the Feb 2026 campaign: the first-ever successful FortiGate authentication from an ASN/geo that had only failures in the baseline window. AWS confirmed 600+ devices fell to this exact shape across 55+ countries. Rationale: Grounded in the article's 'AWS confirmed 600+ devices across 55+ countries' line and the kill-chain hint that first-time-seen ASN+success-after-failure-burst is the campaign's signature. Anti-baseline join is the canonical first-seen detection shape.
ATT&CKT1133 T1078
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Roaming admin connecting from a new hotel / airport ASN they've never used before
  • M&A integration where a newly-acquired sub-org logs in to the parent's appliance for the first time
  • MSP onboarding a new customer tenant from previously-unseen jump-host ASN
  • Carrier-grade-NAT shift moves a fleet of mobile clients to a new ASN block overnight
  • DR test from a backup site whose egress IP is not in the 30-day baseline
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<known_roaming_admin_ips>"])) | where SourceUserName !in~ ("msp-onboarding", "dr-test")
Response runbook
1) Triage: enrich the source IP with ASN/geo + threat-intel; pull the preceding 24 h of failures from the same /24; verify the account is genuinely admin/VPN with management access. 2) Contain: kill the active SSL-VPN tunnel, revoke session cookies, disable the account, and isolate the FortiGate management interface from public reach. 3) Hunt: look for config-change / `exec` CLI bursts from this session, outbound HTTPS from the appliance to LLM-API or unknown JSON-RPC endpoints, and any new admin or local user created in the same window.
let Lookback = 30d;
let Recent = 1h;
let KnownASN = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 4433) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd")
    | summarize by RemoteIP;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(Recent)
| where RemotePort in (443, 10443, 4433)
| join kind=leftanti KnownASN on RemoteIP
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 30d;
let Recent = 1h;
let Baseline = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(Recent))
    | where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
    | where DeviceAction has "success" or Message has_any ("login success", "ssl-vpn-login success")
    | summarize by SourceIP;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(Recent)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where DeviceAction has "success" or Message has_any ("login success", "ssl-vpn-login success")
| where SourceUserName has_any ("admin", "administrator") or Activity has_any ("ssl-vpn", "admin login")
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on SourceIP
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, DeviceExternalID, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) @evt.outcome:success (@msg:("login success" OR "ssl-vpn-login") OR @network.destination.port:(443 OR 10443)) @network.user.name:(admin OR administrator OR *vpn*)

Machine-cadence post-auth FortiGate CLI/API calls in single session (MCP-orchestrated) AIInstallation Medium
Targets the Feb 2026 campaign's signature execution behaviour: an authenticated session that issues many FortiGate CLI/API actions sub-second apart — a cadence no human admin produces — because a custom MCP server is autonomously invoking a curated offensive-tool library against the appliance. Rationale: Article: 'bursts of FortiGate CLI/API calls (config read, diagnose, exec) spaced sub-second apart from a single session — a cadence no human admin produces.' Detection encodes that exact rate/burst signal at the session level rather than alerting on individual commands.
ATT&CKT1059 T1106
Data sourcesChange Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • FortiManager pushing a large policy bundle to the appliance during a scheduled change window
  • Backup / config-export tool (FortiAnalyzer collector, rConfig) pulling running-config via API on cron
  • Authorized BAS or pentest agent enumerating the appliance over the REST API
  • Ansible / Terraform deployment run that idempotent-replays hundreds of `config` blocks
  • Initial provisioning of a new appliance where the engineer pastes a multi-hundred-line config script
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<fortimanager_ip>", "<backup_collector_ip>", "<ansible_runner_ip>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the session's source IP and admin account; check whether FortiManager / approved automation source the burst, and pull the actual command sequence. 2) Contain: terminate the active session, revoke the admin's API token, snapshot the running-config and diff against last-known-good, and block the source IP at the management ACL. 3) Hunt: pivot on the admin account for any new policies, route changes, local user creation, or VPN tunnels added in the burst; check egress from the appliance management plane to LLM/MCP endpoints.
let Window = 1m;
let BurstThreshold = 20;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort in (443, 22, 8443) and InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("httpsd", "sshd", "cli")
| summarize Calls = count(), FirstT = min(Timestamp), LastT = max(Timestamp) by RemoteIP, DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, Window)
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT), RatePerSec = todouble(Calls) / (todouble(datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT)) + 1)
| where Calls >= BurstThreshold and (RatePerSec >= 2.0 or DurationSec <= 10)
| order by Timestamp desc
let Window = 1m;
let BurstThreshold = 20;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet" and DeviceProduct in~ ("FortiGate", "Fortigate")
| where Activity has_any ("config", "exec", "diagnose", "api", "cli") or Message has_any ("exec ", "config ", "diagnose ", "/api/v2/")
| extend SessionKey = strcat(SourceIP, "|", SourceUserName, "|", DeviceExternalID)
| summarize Calls = count(), Cmds = make_set(Activity, 50), FirstT = min(TimeGenerated), LastT = max(TimeGenerated) by SessionKey, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DeviceExternalID, bin(TimeGenerated, Window)
| extend DurationSec = datetime_diff('second', LastT, FirstT)
| extend RatePerSec = todouble(Calls) / (todouble(DurationSec) + 1.0)
| where Calls >= BurstThreshold and (RatePerSec >= 2.0 or DurationSec <= 10)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(linux.syslog OR cisco.firewall) @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate) (@msg:(exec* OR config* OR diagnose* OR "/api/v2/") OR @evt.name:(config_change OR cli_command OR api_call))
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Change.object) as distinct_objects, values(Change.command) as commands, values(Change.object) as objects, min(_time) as first_t, max(_time) as last_t from datamodel=Change where (Change.vendor_product="FortiGate" OR Change.app=fortigate) by Change.user, Change.src, Change.session_id, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | eval duration_s=last_t-first_t, rate_per_s=count/(duration_s+1) | where count>=20 AND (rate_per_s>=2 OR duration_s<=10) | table _time user src session_id count distinct_objects duration_s rate_per_s commands objects
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Change.object) as distinct_objects, values(Change.command) as commands, values(Change.object) as objects, min(_time) as first_t, max(_time) as last_t from datamodel=Change where (Change.vendor_product="FortiGate" OR Change.app=fortigate) by Change.user, Change.src, Change.session_id, _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Change)` | eval duration_s=last_t-first_t, rate_per_s=count/(duration_s+1) | where count>=20 AND (rate_per_s>=2 OR duration_s<=10) | table _time user src session_id count distinct_objects duration_s rate_per_s commands objects
Outbound JSON-RPC or LLM-API egress from network appliance / edge device AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the C2 channel from the Feb 2026 campaign: the custom MCP server brokering tasks between the LLM and compromised FortiGate fleet over HTTPS. Network appliances should never originate AI-API traffic; first-seen FQDN to anthropic / openai / bedrock / unknown JSON-RPC endpoints from edge gear is the tell. Rationale: Article: 'a custom MCP server running offensive tools autonomously' brokering between LLM and compromised devices. Detection ground-truths on the unique behavioural shape — edge appliance originating LLM-API HTTPS — which is essentially zero in any baseline. CloudWatch/VPC-Flow path was dropped because the article-specific telemetry lives on the FortiGate / proxy / DNS layer, not in CloudTrail; emitting an invented VPC-Flow query would be noise.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor support session where a FortiGate streams telemetry through an OpenAI-fronted vendor diagnostic chatbot
  • Legitimate internal SOAR / chatops integration on an appliance management host that genuinely calls an LLM
  • Captive-portal proxy on the appliance forwarding a user's browser session to an LLM provider (rare)
  • Future Fortinet firmware that ships its own AI assistant phoning home to a vendor LLM endpoint
  • DNS resolver on the appliance answering a recursive query for a downstream client (split-horizon misconfig)
Suppression filter
| where DestinationHostName !in~ ("telemetry.fortinet.com", "<approved_vendor_chatops_host>") | where SourceIP !in (dynamic(["<approved_soar_egress_ip>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify which appliance and which management-plane process originated the connection; verify whether the destination FQDN is a known LLM endpoint and whether any vendor change ticket explains it. 2) Contain: block the destination FQDN/IP at the perimeter from all network-appliance source IPs, snapshot the appliance config and running processes, and rotate admin credentials and API tokens on that device. 3) Hunt: correlate with recent admin-login anomalies on the same appliance, look for matching outbound from peer appliances of the same model, and search for inbound JSON-RPC / unusual TLS-SNI patterns that could be the MCP control channel itself.
let LLMHosts = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.anthropic.com", "openai.com", "api.openai.com", "bedrock-runtime", "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", "api.mistral.ai", "api.together.xyz", "api.groq.com", "api.deepseek.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort == 443
| where RemoteUrl has_any (LLMHosts) or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("sslvpnd", "httpsd", "miglogd", "fgfm", "forticron")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe", "brave.exe", "code.exe", "slack.exe", "teams.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let LLMHosts = dynamic(["anthropic.com", "api.anthropic.com", "openai.com", "api.openai.com", "bedrock-runtime", "generativelanguage.googleapis.com", "api.mistral.ai", "api.together.xyz", "api.groq.com", "api.deepseek.com"]);
let ApplianceVendors = dynamic(["Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks", "Cisco", "Check Point", "SonicWall", "Juniper", "F5"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in~ (ApplianceVendors)
| where DestinationPort == 443 or ApplicationProtocol has_any ("https", "ssl", "tls")
| where (isnotempty(DestinationHostName) and DestinationHostName has_any (LLMHosts)) or (isnotempty(RequestURL) and RequestURL has_any (LLMHosts)) or (isnotempty(DestinationDnsDomain) and DestinationDnsDomain has_any (LLMHosts))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceExternalID, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL, Activity, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
| union (
    ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (LLMHosts)
    | where SrcHostname has_any ("fgt", "fortigate", "palo", "asa", "ftd", "checkpoint", "srx", "bigip") or DvcHostname has_any ("fgt", "fortigate", "palo", "asa", "ftd", "checkpoint", "srx", "bigip")
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor=EventVendor, DeviceProduct=EventProduct, DeviceExternalID=DvcHostname, SourceIP=SrcIpAddr, DestinationIP=DstIpAddr, DestinationPort=int(null), DestinationHostName=DstHostname, DestinationDnsDomain=DnsQuery, RequestURL=tostring(""), Activity=tostring("dns_query"), Message=tostring("")
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

(source:(cisco.firewall OR linux.syslog OR fortinet.fortigate OR paloaltonetworks.firewall) OR @source.product:(fortigate OR FortiGate OR PAN-OS OR ASA OR FTD)) (@network.destination.port:443 OR @network.protocol:https) (@dns.question.name:(*anthropic.com OR *openai.com OR bedrock-runtime* OR generativelanguage.googleapis.com OR api.mistral.ai OR api.together.xyz OR api.groq.com OR api.deepseek.com) OR @http.url:(*anthropic.com* OR *openai.com* OR *bedrock-runtime* OR *generativelanguage.googleapis.com*) OR @network.destination.domain:(*anthropic.com OR *openai.com))

| tstats summariesonly=false count, sum(Network_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out, values(Network_Traffic.dest_host) as dest_hosts, values(Network_Traffic.ssl_subject) as sni from datamodel=Network_Traffic where (Network_Traffic.src_category="network_appliance" OR Network_Traffic.src_category="firewall" OR Network_Traffic.src_category="edge_router") Network_Traffic.dest_port=443 by Network_Traffic.src, Network_Traffic.dest_host, _time span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Network_Traffic)` | search dest_host IN ("*anthropic.com", "*openai.com", "*bedrock-runtime*.amazonaws.com", "*generativelanguage.googleapis.com", "*api.mistral.ai", "*api.together.xyz", "*api.groq.com", "*api.deepseek.com") OR sni IN ("*anthropic.com", "*openai.com") | table _time src dest_host sni count bytes_out
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors With SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 16 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Vietnam-aligned threat actor known as OceanLotus has been attributed to two distinct campaigns that targeted domestic entities and stock investors with a backdoor known as SPECTRALVIPER. The campaigns involve a prolonged cyber espionage operation aimed at a Vietnamese infrastructure and transport construction corporation between mid-2024 and February 2026, as well as a supply chain attack

FireAnt Metakit supply-chain update download from metakit.fireant.vn AIDelivery High
Hunts the OceanLotus FireAnt supply-chain compromise where the legitimate Metakit.exe updater fetched a tampered setup.exe from the vendor's own update channel (metakit.fireant[.]vn/Software/version.xml) due to absent signature validation. Surfaces the unique parent->child download pattern between Oct 2025 and Mar 2026. Rationale: Anchors on the article's named binary chain (Metakit.exe -> setup.exe), the exact update URL path (metakit.fireant[.]vn/Software/version.xml) and the IOC SHA1 set. The parent/child pivot between two specific FireAnt binaries makes this near-zero FP outside the FireAnt user base. Image [3] also shows the update flow. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate FireAnt Metakit updates after the vendor restored signature validation (post-March 2026)
  • Security researchers replaying the campaign in a sandbox
  • IR tools (CrowdStrike RTR, MDE Live Response) replaying setup.exe for triage
  • Endpoint backup tools copying setup.exe between hosts
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Veeam\", @"\CrowdStrike\", @"\WindowsApps\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm Metakit.exe exists at the standard FireAnt install path, capture setup.exe and hash it against the IOC SHA1 set; pull DeviceFileEvents for the SHA256 across the fleet. 2) Contain: isolate the host via MDE/CrowdStrike, block metakit.fireant.vn at the proxy if the host is not a legitimate FireAnt user, kill running OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe, snapshot memory. 3) Hunt: pivot on the SHA1/SHA256 across all DeviceFileEvents, sweep DeviceNetworkEvents for connections to financemachinelearning[.]com and the rest of the C2 set, and review InitiatingProcessParentFileName trees originating from any DtlCrashCatch.dll loader.
let lookback = 180d;
let badHashes = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D","B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194","48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947","511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB","8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
let downloads = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where RemoteUrl has "metakit.fireant.vn" or RemoteUrl has "/Software/version.xml"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl, NetProcId = InitiatingProcessId, NetParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
let drops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
    | where FileName =~ "setup.exe" or SHA1 in~ (badHashes)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
| where FileName =~ "setup.exe" or SHA1 in~ (badHashes)
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA1, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| union downloads, drops
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 180d;
let badHashes = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D","B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194","48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947","511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB","8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where ParentProcessName has "Metakit.exe"
    | where ActingProcessName has "setup.exe" or SHA1 in~ (badHashes)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=ActorUsername, Parent=ParentProcessName, Child=ActingProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA1, Source="ImProcessCreate"),
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)

    | where ParentProcessName has "Metakit.exe"
    | where NewProcessName has "setup.exe" or FileHash in~ (badHashes)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, Actor=Account, Parent=ParentProcessName, Child=NewProcessName, Cmd=CommandLine, SHA1=FileHash, Source="SecurityEvent"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where Url has "metakit.fireant.vn" or Url has "/Software/version.xml"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=SrcUsername, Parent="", Child="", Cmd=Url, SHA1="", Source="ImWebSession")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: OceanLotus FireAnt Metakit Supply-Chain Updater Drop
id: 8a2c1b5d-7e3f-4a9d-b2a1-1c0e9f6a4b21
description: Detects Metakit.exe (FireAnt stock investor platform) spawning setup.exe as a child or fetching the unsigned version.xml/setup.exe pair from the legitimate-but-abused metakit.fireant.vn update channel during OceanLotus's Oct-2025 to Mar-2026 supply-chain campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\Metakit.exe'
    Image|endswith: '\setup.exe'
  selection_hash:
    Hashes|contains:
      - '865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D'
      - 'B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194'
      - '48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947'
      - '511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB'
      - '8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037'
  condition: selection or selection_hash
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\Metakit.exe OR *\METAKIT.EXE OR *\metakit.exe) AND @Image:(*\setup.exe OR *\SETUP.EXE OR *\Setup.exe)) OR @Hashes:(*865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D* OR *B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194* OR *48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947* OR *511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB* OR *8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^metakit\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\setup\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe" (Processes.process_name="setup.exe" OR Processes.process IN ("*metakit.fireant.vn*","*Software/version.xml*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="Metakit.exe" (Processes.process_name="setup.exe" OR Processes.process IN ("*metakit.fireant.vn*","*Software/version.xml*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
DtlCrashCatch.dll side-loaded into signed binary (SPECTRALVIPER side-load DLL) AIInstallation High
Hunts the SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load primitive where a legitimate signed binary loads the rogue DtlCrashCatch.dll, which subsequently injects into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe. The DLL filename is uncommon and ESET-published — a direct image-load hit is high-confidence. Rationale: DtlCrashCatch.dll is a campaign-unique filename published by ESET specifically for this OceanLotus side-load chain. A bare image-load hit against this DLL name is therefore high-fidelity with no behavioural noise required. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1574/002/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1055.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • ESET / vendor researcher replaying the IOC on a research host
  • Defender ASR sample-submission environments
  • IR engagement tooling staging the DLL for analysis
  • Yara/sandbox scanning systems containing samples on disk
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash DtlCrashCatch.dll on disk, identify the parent signed binary that loaded it (InitiatingProcessFileName) and whether OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe is showing follow-on injection. 2) Contain: isolate host, kill OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe, quarantine the DLL and its loader binary, preserve memory dump for SPECTRALVIPER artefacts. 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for the DLL filename + SHA256, pivot DeviceNetworkEvents to financemachinelearning[.]com / gatewayrvcenter[.]com from any host that loaded the DLL, and check for the FireAnt Metakit installer trail upstream.
let lookback = 180d;
let loaders = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll" or FolderPath has "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, DllPath = FolderPath, DllSHA256 = SHA256,
              LoaderProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName, LoaderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              LoaderCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, LoaderSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
              Source = "ImageLoad";
let drops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, DllPath = FolderPath, DllSHA256 = SHA256,
              LoaderProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName, LoaderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              LoaderCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, LoaderSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
              Source = "FileWrite";
loaders
| union drops
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 180d;
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where TargetFileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll" or TargetFilePath has "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=ActorUsername, LoaderProcess=ActingProcessName, LoaderCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, DllPath=TargetFilePath, DllSHA256=TargetFileSHA256, Source="ImFileEvent"),
  (Event
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 7
    | where EventData has "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, Actor=UserName, LoaderProcess="", LoaderCmd="", DllPath=tostring(EventData), DllSHA256="", Source="Sysmon-EID7")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SPECTRALVIPER injection into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe AIInstallation Medium
Detects the SPECTRALVIPER stage where the side-loaded DtlCrashCatch.dll injects into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe - which then makes the actual C2 connection. Catches both injection telemetry and the unusual post-injection network behaviour of a normally-cloud-only binary contacting non-Microsoft destinations. Rationale: ESET explicitly names OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe as the injected host for SPECTRALVIPER. That binary should only ever talk to Microsoft cloud endpoints - any public destination that's not in the Microsoft allowlist (especially the article's named C2s) is a strong signal. Pairs neatly with DtlCrashCatch.dll DLL load on the same host. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/spectralviper
ATT&CKT1055 T1055.012
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Corporate proxies that NAT OneDrive traffic through third-party CDN edges
  • OneDrive interacting with internal SharePoint endpoints not in default allowlist
  • SCCM/Intune endpoint analytics shipping OneDrive telemetry
  • Custom OneDrive sync clients in dev/test environments
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("microsoft.com","live.com","officeapps.live.com","onedrive.com","sharepoint.com","office.net"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe's parent and module list - look for DtlCrashCatch.dll, unsigned modules, or RWX regions; verify the remote destination isn't a legitimate Microsoft CDN edge. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate the OneDrive process tree, block outbound to the contacted IP/domain, snapshot memory for the SPECTRALVIPER reflective payload. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceImageLoadEvents on the host for DtlCrashCatch.dll, run the FireAnt Metakit UC fleet-wide, and sweep DeviceNetworkEvents over 180 days for any process connecting to the same C2 IPs/domains.
let lookback = 30d;
let msAllow = dynamic(["microsoft.com","live.com","office.com","officeapps.live.com","onedrive.com","sharepointonline.com","sharepoint.com","office.net","msocdn.com","msftauth.net","cdn.onenote.net"]);
let c2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let c2IPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
let odNet = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
    | extend DomainMatch = iff(isnotempty(RemoteUrl), tolower(RemoteUrl), "")
    | where (isnotempty(RemoteUrl) and not(DomainMatch has_any (msAllow))) or RemoteUrl has_any (c2Domains) or RemoteIP in (c2IPs)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source="Network";
let odInject = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where ActionType in ("CreateRemoteThreadApiCall","ReadProcessMemoryApiCall","OpenProcessApiCall")
    | where FileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("OneDrive.exe","OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe","OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl="", RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(null), Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source=ActionType;
odNet
| union odInject
| order by Timestamp desc

SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure contact (any process, IOC sweep) AICommand & Control Medium
Sweeps any host process touching the ESET-published SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure (financemachinelearning[.]com, gatewayrvcenter[.]com, the four secondary domains, and the eight IP IOCs). Casts a wide net by process - SPECTRALVIPER can inject into multiple host binaries on the same machine. Rationale: Pure IOC sweep against the eight IPs and six domains published by ESET; high-confidence and process-agnostic so it catches SPECTRALVIPER regardless of which host process it injects into. Sentinel KQL union covers DnsEvents (Computer), CommonSecurityLog (SourceHostName), ImDnsActivity (DvcHostname) and ImNetworkSession (DvcHostname) - each table projects its own host column rather than referencing DeviceName which only exists on Defender-XDR Device* tables. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/ • https://otx.alienvault.com/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel researchers/sandboxes actively detonating SPECTRALVIPER samples
  • Internal sinkhole or DNS RPZ logging the lookup before blocking
  • Honeypot/deception platforms intentionally talking to the IOCs
  • Stale DNS cache lookups on rebuilt hosts hitting previously-known infrastructure
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the process making the contact (InitiatingProcessFileName) and check whether DtlCrashCatch.dll or the FireAnt Metakit chain exists on the host - they should be present upstream. 2) Contain: isolate the host, push the domain/IP set into the perimeter blocklist, and revoke any user credentials cached on the host. 3) Hunt: sweep DNS logs across the org for the same domains, check passive DNS for related infrastructure (same name servers, shared cert), and search for any process that loaded DtlCrashCatch.dll or descended from Metakit.exe.
let lookback = 180d;
let c2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let c2IPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where RemoteIP in (c2IPs)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (c2Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc

union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where Name in~ (c2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ClientIP, RemoteHost=Name, RemoteIP="", Source="DnsEvents"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where DestinationHostName in~ (c2Domains) or DestinationIP in (c2IPs)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, RemoteHost=DestinationHostName, RemoteIP=DestinationIP, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where DnsQuery in~ (c2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, RemoteHost=DnsQuery, RemoteIP="", Source="ImDnsActivity"),
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where DstHostname in~ (c2Domains) or DstIpAddr in (c2IPs)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, RemoteHost=DstHostname, RemoteIP=DstIpAddr, Source="ImNetworkSession")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Known SPECTRALVIPER sample hash hit (file write or process execute) AIInstallation Medium
Hash-based IOC sweep for the five SHA1 samples ESET attributed to SPECTRALVIPER and the FireAnt Metakit dropper. Trivially deployable, near-zero FP outside research environments, and catches the artefacts even if filenames or paths get changed in future variants. Rationale: Pure SHA1 IOC sweep against the five article-published hashes - the union covers process exec, file writes and DLL loads, so the detection fires whether SPECTRALVIPER lands as a binary, gets injected as a DLL, or is staged on disk before execution. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/ • https://otx.alienvault.com/
ATT&CKT1027 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AV/EDR vendors hashing the IOC for sample validation
  • Security researchers manually loading samples for analysis
  • IR engagement teams importing the SHA1 set into hunt tools
  • Honeypot/range environments hosting the samples for training
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the hash is not a researcher/sandbox host, capture the binary plus parent process context. 2) Contain: isolate, quarantine the file, kill the loader chain (Metakit.exe / OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe), and dump memory for SPECTRALVIPER reflective payload. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceFileEvents on the same SHA256, run the C2 IOC sweep on the host, and walk the parent-chain back to FireAnt update activity or MSSQL exploitation.
let lookback = 180d;
let iocs = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D","B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194","48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947","511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB","8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where SHA1 in~ (iocs) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in~ (iocs)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine, ParentFile=InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="ProcessEvents"),
  (DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where SHA1 in~ (iocs) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in~ (iocs)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ParentFile=InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="FileEvents"),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
    | where SHA1 in~ (iocs)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ParentFile=InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="ImageLoad")
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 180d;
let iocs = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D","B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194","48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947","511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB","8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where TargetFileSHA1 in~ (iocs) or Hash in~ (iocs)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=ActorUsername, FileName=TargetFileName, FilePath=TargetFilePath, SHA1=TargetFileSHA1, Source="ImFileEvent"),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where SHA1 in~ (iocs)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=ActorUsername, FileName=ActingProcessName, FilePath=ActingProcessName, SHA1, Source="ImProcessCreate"),
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where EventID == 4688 and FileHash in~ (iocs)
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, Actor=Account, FileName=NewProcessName, FilePath=NewProcessName, SHA1=FileHash, Source="SecurityEvent")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Public-facing MSSQL spawning shell or LOLBin (OceanLotus T-Construction TTPs) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the suspected initial-access vector for OceanLotus's Vietnamese transport-construction intrusion - exploitation of public-facing Microsoft SQL Server leading to sqlservr.exe spawning interactive shells, LOLBins or PowerShell. Covers Nov 2024 to Feb 2026 dwell time. Rationale: ESET assesses initial access for the transport-construction intrusion as MSSQL RCE; sqlservr.exe spawning interactive shells or LOLBins is the textbook post-exploitation primitive for that vector. Machine-account exclusion (per anti-bad-account-filter) keeps SQL Agent service noise out. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.003 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DBA running xp_cmdshell for legitimate ETL / housekeeping scripts
  • SQL Agent jobs invoking PowerShell for backups or report generation
  • SCCM/Configuration Manager calling cmd.exe from inside SQL Reporting Services
  • Patch automation tooling running net.exe/sc.exe via xp_cmdshell
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("SQLAgent","Backup","Maintenance","Replication")) | where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"D:\\SQLBackups"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify whether xp_cmdshell or CLR-integration is enabled on the instance, confirm whether the spawning user is a DBA service account vs sa, capture the full process tree including the SQL session origin (sourceIP, login name). 2) Contain: disable xp_cmdshell on the instance, restrict the MSSQL listener at the firewall, force a sa password rotation, snapshot the SQL host for forensics. 3) Hunt: sweep DeviceFileEvents for DtlCrashCatch.dll across all hosts, pivot DeviceNetworkEvents for the SPECTRALVIPER C2 IOC set, and review MSSQL audit logs (errorlog, default trace) for login activity from external IPs over the dwell window.
let lookback = 30d;
let lolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","wmic.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","hostname.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","curl.exe","ftp.exe","sc.exe","reg.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sqlservr.exe"
| where FileName in~ (lolbins)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let lookback = 30d;
let lolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","wmic.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","hostname.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","curl.exe","ftp.exe","sc.exe","reg.exe"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName has "sqlservr.exe"
    | extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
    | where ChildName in (lolbins)
    | where Account !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, Actor=Account, Parent=ParentProcessName, Child=NewProcessName, Cmd=CommandLine, Source="SecurityEvent"),
  (ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where ParentProcessName has "sqlservr.exe"
    | extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(ActingProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
    | where ChildName in (lolbins)
    | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
    | project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=ActorUsername, Parent=ParentProcessName, Child=ActingProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Source="ImProcessCreate")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: MSSQL Server Spawning Shell or LOLBin
id: 4d8a2f1c-6b3e-4a1d-8e9c-2b7d4c8a3e51
description: Detects sqlservr.exe spawning interactive shells or LOLBins - suspected initial-access path for the OceanLotus intrusion against the Vietnamese transport-construction firm (Nov 2024-Feb 2026), where ESET attributes initial entry to MSSQL RCE.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:

  - attack.execution

  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\sqlservr.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'

      - '\whoami.exe'

      - '\systeminfo.exe'
      - '\tasklist.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\ftp.exe'
  filter:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection and not filter
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\sqlservr.exe OR *\SQLSERVR.EXE OR *\Sqlservr.exe) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\RunDLL32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\WMIC.EXE OR *\net.exe OR *\whoami.exe OR *\hostname.exe OR *\systeminfo.exe OR *\tasklist.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\ftp.exe) -@User:*$

| NOT UserName=/\$$/

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

| sort - count

    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

status: experimental
description: |

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/

    product: windows

    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'

        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:

            - 'invoke-expression'

        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit supply-chain: update binary spawning unusual child
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OceanLotus: From external espionage to domestic targeting
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER known-sample SHA1 execution or filesystem write · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 connection to ESET-disclosed IPs/domains · [LLM] First-seen connection to recently-registered SPECTRALVIPER-shape C2 domain · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 connection to ESET-disclosed IPs/domains AICommand & Control Medium
Alerts on any outbound network connection to the eight SPECTRALVIPER C2 IPs and six C&C domains ESET published for OceanLotus's 2024-2026 FireAnt Metakit supply-chain and Vietnamese construction-corp campaigns. High-fidelity because every IOC is a known-bad C2 endpoint with no documented benign use. Rationale: Every IP and domain in this query is a SPECTRALVIPER C&C endpoint published in ESET's Table 2 and IOC bundle for the 2024-2026 OceanLotus campaigns; financemachinelearning.com is explicitly named as the C&C domain for the stable SPECTRALVIPER variant. Match by IP catches direct fallback; match by URL catches HTTPS proxied through hostname.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandbox / malware-analysis VM intentionally detonating SPECTRALVIPER samples
  • Threat-intel scrapers / Shodan-style researchers actively probing the IOC set
  • Security-tool URL-categorization scans of the malicious domains (e.g. Zscaler, Netskope)
  • Legitimate hosts that happen to be on a shared-IP CDN that now resolves to one of these IPs (rare — most IOCs are bare hosting)
  • DNS sinkhole responses if these domains have been sinkholed by a TI provider
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files\\" or InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","iexplore.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the full process tree from DeviceProcessEvents for InitiatingProcessFileName at the time of the connection — confirm whether the originator is a known good binary (security tooling, sandbox) or an unsigned binary in a temp/AppData path matching SPECTRALVIPER drop patterns. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the device via Defender Live Response or EDR network-isolation, block the matched IP/domain at firewall and EDR network indicator policy, force credential reset for the InitiatingProcessAccountName. 3) HUNT: pivot on DeviceFileEvents for SHA1 against the 20-hash IOC set; query DnsEvents for the other five C&C domains across all hosts in the last 90 days; search for any FireAnt Metakit installs (file path or process name) on neighboring hosts and check their update history for a malicious payload window of Oct-2025 to Mar-2026.

let ioc_domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256

SPECTRALVIPER known-sample SHA1 execution or filesystem write AIInstallation High
Alerts whenever a process executes or a file is written whose SHA1 matches one of the 20 SPECTRALVIPER / OceanLotus stager and dropper hashes ESET published. Covers both SPECTRALVIPER backdoor binaries and the malicious FireAnt Metakit update payloads from the supply-chain wave. Rationale: All 20 SHA1s are pulled directly from the IOC block of the ESET report and correspond to SPECTRALVIPER samples (both old reused first-iteration samples and fresh stable-version samples from Table 1) plus the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain droppers. Hash match on process + filesystem + image-load catches dropper, persistent loader, and DLL side-load variants.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1027 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender / CrowdStrike sample-submission VMs ingesting the IOC bundle for testing
  • DFIR teams replaying confirmed malware samples during tabletop exercises
  • VirusTotal / hybrid-analysis collector hosts that store hash archives
  • Security researcher endpoints reverse-engineering the samples
  • Backup/restore restoring a previously-quarantined sample from shadow copy
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !has "sandbox" and DeviceName !has "malware" and DeviceName !has "detonation"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: identify whether the host is a known malware-analysis sandbox or a production endpoint — check device tags, OU membership and the user profile of InitiatingProcessAccountName. If production, this is a confirmed-malicious detection with no investigation needed before action. 2) CONTAIN: network-isolate the device, kill the process tree, quarantine the binary, force credential rotation for any account with an interactive logon to that host in the last 90 days, and block the SHA1 across the EDR fleet via Indicators of Compromise policy. 3) HUNT: for every host that ran one of these hashes, pull DeviceNetworkEvents and DnsEvents 30 days back looking for the six SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains and eight IPs; check FireAnt Metakit install history; pivot on the InitiatingProcessFolderPath to identify the dropper that wrote the sample.

union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where SHA1 in~ (ioc_sha1) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in~ (ioc_sha1)
  | project Timestamp, Table="Process", DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine),
