FireAnt Metakit supply-chain: update binary spawning unusual child AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for the FireAnt Metakit application (the Vietnamese stock-investment platform whose update server OceanLotus compromised from Oct-2025 to Mar-2026) spawning script interpreters, LOLBins, or unsigned binaries from temp/AppData. This is the textbook detection shape for the supply-chain payload that ESET observed delivering SPECTRALVIPER after a poisoned update. Rationale: ESET explicitly names FireAnt Metakit as the compromised stock-trading platform and describes the update-server-replaced-with-malicious-payload pattern; any FireAnt Metakit process spawning a script interpreter, LOLBin, or binary out of temp/AppData is the operational shape of the supply-chain payload chain that ends in SPECTRALVIPER drop. Hunting tier because FireAnt's own update process may legitimately invoke some installer LOLBins on first install.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate FireAnt Metakit update invoking msiexec.exe during a real product update
  • FireAnt installer writing helper binaries to %TEMP% as part of normal first-run installation
  • Endpoint backup software (Veeam, Acronis) interacting with FireAnt install directory during scheduled backup
  • User troubleshooting FireAnt by running it from a portable/extracted location in Downloads
  • Antivirus / DLP scanning FireAnt binaries on a schedule and reading from AppData
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessSignatureStatus != "Valid" or ChildSHA256 !in~ (toscalar(DeviceFileCertificateInfo | where IsSigned == true and SignatureType == "CodeSign" | summarize make_set(SHA256)))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the FireAnt Metakit installer SHA256 and version from InitiatingProcessSHA256 / VersionInfoProductVersion and compare against the vendor's published known-good hash; check the timestamp against ESET's Oct-2025 to Mar-2026 supply-chain window — any install in that range is suspect by default. 2) CONTAIN: if the parent SHA256 is unknown or in the known-bad set, isolate the host, kill the process tree, and quarantine all files written by the child process in the prior 24h; alert the user to discontinue use of FireAnt Metakit pending vendor confirmation. 3) HUNT: query DeviceNetworkEvents on the host for any of the six SPECTRALVIPER C2 domains in the 7 days after the install; pivot DeviceFileEvents for files written by InitiatingProcessFolderPath of FireAnt to identify dropped stagers; check for any other endpoints in the org running FireAnt and audit their install times.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "fireant" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has "fireant"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where ParentProcessName has "fireant" or ActingProcessName has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit") or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("FireAnt","Metakit")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","msiexec.exe")
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA1, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit Supply-Chain Update Spawning Suspicious Child
id: 9f1c5e22-3a7d-4f44-8e91-2f4a8b9c0d11
description: Detects the FireAnt Metakit Vietnamese stock-investment platform spawning script interpreters, LOLBins, or binaries from temp/AppData. ESET attributes a compromised-update-server supply-chain attack (Oct 2025 - Mar 2026) on this product to OceanLotus / APT32 that resulted in SPECTRALVIPER deployment.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - 'FireAnt'
      - 'Metakit'
  suspicious_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  suspicious_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\AppData\Roaming\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
  condition: parent and (suspicious_child or suspicious_path)
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) @EventID:(1 OR 4688) (@ParentImage:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit* OR *metakit*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit*)) (@Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\wget.exe OR *\msiexec.exe) OR @Image:(*\AppData\Local\Temp\* OR *\AppData\Roaming\* OR *\ProgramData\* OR *\Windows\Temp\* OR *\Users\Public\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/fireant|metakit/i OR ParentImageFileName=/(FireAnt|Metakit)/i
| (ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget|msiexec)\.exe$/i OR regex("\\\\(AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|AppData\\\\Roaming|ProgramData|Windows\\\\Temp|Users\\\\Public)\\\\", field=ImageFileName))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="*fireant*" OR Processes.parent_process="*FireAnt*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Metakit*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="*fireant*" OR Processes.parent_process="*FireAnt*" OR Processes.parent_process="*Metakit*") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
First-seen connection to recently-registered SPECTRALVIPER-shape C2 domain AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for any internal host making a first-time HTTPS connection to a domain matching the SPECTRALVIPER C&C naming pattern ESET catalogued (single-word .com domains posing as services - finance/cyber/sync/design themed), where the domain is unseen across the org's 30-day baseline. Designed to catch the next OceanLotus C2 rotation before the IOC list updates. Rationale: Uses the explicit six SPECTRALVIPER C&C domains from ESET Table 2 AND a baseline anti-join so any first-time-in-org connection to a similarly-shaped domain (finance/cyber/services themed single-word .coms — the OceanLotus naming convention) gets flagged. Catches IOC rotation that won't be in the next ESET update.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Marketing/finance department visiting a newly-launched legitimate fintech site for the first time
  • User clicking a phishing-link analysis service that proxies through similar-shape domains
  • Threat-intel browser extension fetching from a sandbox URL
  • Internal CI/CD reaching a newly-provisioned vendor SaaS subdomain
  • Domain typosquats of legitimate companies (separate detection class)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe","opera.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: enrich the matched domain with WHOIS / registration date and passive DNS - any domain registered in the last 90 days with low passive-DNS history and matching the SPECTRALVIPER naming theme is high-suspicion; check InitiatingProcessFileName to see whether it's a browser (often FP) or an unsigned binary (almost always TP). 2) CONTAIN: if non-browser process or unsigned binary, isolate the host, sinkhole the domain via DNS RPZ, and block at proxy/firewall; if browser, push the URL to your secure-browsing/SWG block-list pending vendor categorization. 3) HUNT: across the fleet, search the last 90 days for any prior connection to the same domain or any of the six known SPECTRALVIPER C&Cs; pivot on the matched host for any of the 20 SHA1 SPECTRALVIPER hashes and for FireAnt Metakit install activity.
let BaselineDomains = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
    | extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(DeviceId) by Domain
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_pattern = @"(?i)(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$";
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Domain = tolower(tostring(split(RemoteUrl, "/")[2]))
| where Domain matches regex ioc_pattern or Domain matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on Domain
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, Domain, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let BaselineDomains = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | summarize HostCount = dcount(SrcIpAddr) by DnsQuery=tolower(DnsQuery)
    | where HostCount > 2;
let ioc_known = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let shape_pattern = @"(?i)\b(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign|services|teams)\b";
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| extend DnsQueryLower = tolower(DnsQuery)
| where DnsQueryLower has_any (ioc_known) or DnsQueryLower matches regex shape_pattern
| join kind=leftanti BaselineDomains on $left.DnsQueryLower == $right.DnsQuery
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) @EventID:22 (@QueryName:(*financemachinelearning.com OR *gatewayrvcenter.com OR *coachcybersecurity.com OR *mxprodesign.com OR *power-sync-services.com OR *leadingfilipinoteams.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(financemachinelearning|gatewayrvcenter|coachcybersecurity|mxprodesign|power-sync-services|leadingfilipinoteams)\.com$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, FirstIP4Record], function=count(), function=min(@timestamp))
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where DNS.query IN ("*financemachinelearning.com","*gatewayrvcenter.com","*coachcybersecurity.com","*mxprodesign.com","*power-sync-services.com","*leadingfilipinoteams.com") OR DNS.query="*" by DNS.src DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | join type=left query [ | tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) as firstSeenOrg from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d by DNS.query | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` ] | where isnull(firstSeenOrg) AND (match(query,"(?i)(finance|cyber|sync|design|machinelearning|filipino|gateway|rvcenter|prodesign).*\.com$")) | sort 0 -count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241") or RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

let BadDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
ImNetworkSession

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:

            - '\paexec.exe'

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"

        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("D511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39F", "59A8553A4F8130F576AB234E0B220BE4D4DA0E98", "9CA1A5C7F79882DB913534C1E62B26BCDCB9F6DD",        Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]
High

GitHub to Disable npm Install Scripts by Default to Stop Supply Chain Attacks

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 11 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

GitHub has announced what it said are "breaking changes" coming to npm version 12, one of which turns off install scripts by default to combat software supply chain threats. The changes aim to combat attack techniques that abuse the "npm install" command to trigger the execution of malicious code using npm lifecycle hooks. "Npm install" is used to download and install all the necessary

npm or yarn lifecycle hook spawning interpreter or LOLBin AIInstallation Medium
Hunts npm/yarn/pnpm install processes spawning script interpreters or LOLBins — the exact pattern GitHub flagged when describing install-time lifecycle scripts as the 'single largest code-execution surface in the npm ecosystem'. Captures the parent (package manager + install verb) and child (powershell/cmd/wscript/curl/certutil) combination that turns a poisoned transitive dependency into RCE. Rationale: Anchors on the exact strings the article names: 'preinstall, install, postinstall', the 'npm install' command, and the GitHub claim that lifecycle scripts are 'the single largest code-execution surface'. Article-specific because it pairs the npm/yarn/pnpm parent + install verb with the LOLBin child set.
ATT&CKT1059 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • electron-builder / husky postinstall legitimately spawning powershell or cmd for hook setup
  • CI runner invoking npm test which shells out via cmd /c
  • node-gyp rebuild of bcrypt/sqlite3/sharp spawning python.exe and msbuild.exe
  • developer running npm ci that chains a custom shell script defined in package.json scripts
  • cross-env / npm-run-all wrapping a downstream command in cmd.exe
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","electron-rebuild","husky install","prebuild-install") and FileName in~ ("python.exe","cmd.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the full process tree — grab ParentCommandLine to identify which package's lifecycle hook fired, and walk up to the originating user shell or CI runner. Pivot on SHA256 of the child via Defender + VT. Step 2 (contain): isolate the developer/CI host; flag the implicated package@version in the artifact registry; force-rotate any developer credentials (.env, .aws, .ssh, git tokens) that lived on the box. Step 3 (hunt): search DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound connections by the same parent process group in the +/-5 min window; pivot on the package name across other hosts to find blast radius; check internal registry mirror for the same version pulled by other projects.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","npm.cmd","yarn.cmd")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","postinstall","preinstall"," ci ","prepare")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","bash.exe","python.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","npm.cmd","yarn.cmd")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","postinstall","preinstall"," ci ","prepare")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","bash.exe","python.exe")
| where not (ActorUsername endswith "$")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\yarn.cmd'
  selection_parent_cmd:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'install'
      - 'postinstall'
      - 'preinstall'
      - 'prepare'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'

level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\Yarn.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe) @ParentCommandLine:(*install* OR *Install* OR *postinstall* OR *preinstall* OR *prepare*) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe)

| regex("(?i)(install|postinstall|preinstall|prepare)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|curl|wget|certutil|bitsadmin|bash|python)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

Suspicious writes into node_modules outside of package-manager processes AIInstallation Medium
Surfaces writes of executable or script content into node_modules paths by processes other than the npm/yarn/pnpm/git/IDE allow-list. Targets post-install tampering and malicious payload drops into a JS dependency tree — a behaviour orthogonal to install-time hook execution that survives the npm v12 default-deny. Rationale: Article frames install-time hooks as the principal execution surface; this UC covers the orthogonal pivot of someone (or something) writing into a dependency tree without npm. Anchors on the exact path token 'node_modules' and the script/native-binary extension family JS packages execute at runtime.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • webpack/Vite/esbuild dev-server emitting cache or HMR artifacts into node_modules/.cache
  • patch-package or pnpm patch rewriting installed package files
  • yarn workspaces / npm link replacing files via symlink/copy
  • TypeScript compiler emitting .js into nested node_modules/@types
  • Renovate/Dependabot CI runners using non-allowlisted wrappers
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\.bin\",@"\node_modules\.cache\") and FileName endswith ".js")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify the writing process and its parent chain — confirm it's not a known dev tooling extension (patch-package, esbuild). Hash the dropped file and check VT plus internal package registry. Step 2 (contain): quarantine the file, isolate the host if the dropper is a non-build process (powershell, cmd, rundll32). Wipe and reinstall node_modules from lockfile after confirming clean state. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the package directory name to find the same dropped artifact across other developer hosts and CI runners; check git history for any tampered commits referencing the same path.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","git.exe","tar.exe","code.exe","tsc.exe","Code.exe")
| where FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".node" or FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".sh" or FileName endswith ".ps1" or FileName endswith ".bat" or FileName endswith ".vbs"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","git.exe","tar.exe","code.exe","tsc.exe"))
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("js","node","exe","dll","sh","ps1","bat","vbs")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileExtension, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

npm install child process accessing credential stores (.env, .ssh, .aws) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects npm/yarn/pnpm install descendants whose command line targets developer credential locations — .env, .ssh, .aws/credentials, .npmrc, id_rsa, .docker/config, gh hosts.yml. Matches the well-documented postinstall-theft pattern the article warns about when it describes a 'compromised package anywhere in the dependency tree' running arbitrary code on developer or CI machines. Rationale: Article's threat model — 'a single compromised package anywhere in the dependency tree can run arbitrary code on a developer machine or CI runner' — is exactly the credential-theft postinstall pattern. Anchors on the canonical credential paths plus the install/postinstall verb in the parent command line.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Webpack DefinePlugin / Vite env loader reading .env at build time
  • aws-sdk picking up ~/.aws/credentials during integration tests
  • dotenv-cli wrapping a build script with -e .env
  • npm package version-bump script reading .npmrc for registry config
  • gh-cli prebuilt action checking ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml during CI
Suppression filter
and not (FileName in~ ("webpack.exe","vite.exe","dotenv.exe","gh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--mode","--config","auth status"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): inspect ActingProcessCommandLine for the credential path; confirm whether the child is a known build tool (webpack, dotenv-cli) or a generic shell/curl/node. Identify the parent package by walking the npm logs. Step 2 (contain): isolate host; force-rotate any exposed credentials (.env tokens, AWS keys, SSH keys, GH PAT, npm tokens); revoke npm publish tokens if the user is a maintainer. Step 3 (hunt): search DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound POSTs / DNS exfil by the same process tree in the next 15 min; pivot on the implicated package@version across artifact registry, internal mirrors, and other developer hosts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","postinstall","preinstall"," ci ")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".env",".ssh",".aws\\credentials",".aws/credentials",".npmrc","id_rsa",".docker\\config",".docker/config","gh\\hosts.yml","gh/hosts.yml")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","postinstall","preinstall"," ci ")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".env",".ssh",".aws\\credentials",".aws/credentials",".npmrc","id_rsa",".docker\\config",".docker/config","gh\\hosts.yml","gh/hosts.yml")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Modification of package.json scripts or .npmrc by non-developer-tool process AIInstallation Medium
Detects creation or modification of package.json or .npmrc files by processes outside the developer-tool allow list. Directly tracks the attack surface GitHub flagged: the article calls out that '.npmrc configuration file used could override the Git executable, even with --ignore-scripts', and package.json scripts are the entry point for the preinstall/install/postinstall hooks being disabled by default in npm v12. Rationale: Article explicitly names .npmrc as a code-execution path that bypasses --ignore-scripts, and package.json scripts are the lifecycle-hook surface being locked down. Anchors on those exact file names plus an allow-list of legitimate editors/package-managers.
ATT&CKT1546 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • npm version patch / yarn version writing package.json
  • Renovate / Dependabot bot rewriting package.json + lockfile on automated PR
  • CI pipeline using sed/jq to inject build-time fields into package.json
  • custom in-house generator (nx, lerna) regenerating workspace package.json
  • developer using a non-mainstream editor (sublime_text, atom, helix) the allowlist hasn't captured
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm version","yarn version","renovate","dependabot") )
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): diff the file against git HEAD — look for added preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare entries, new dependencies pointing at git+https or http(s) tarballs, or new .npmrc lines invoking a custom script-shell or git executable. Step 2 (contain): revert the change, isolate host if the writer is a shell/curl/powershell; force npm token rotation if any new install hook ran. Step 3 (hunt): search for the same suspicious script string across the repo and across other developer hosts; check the artifact registry for any newly published versions in the past 24h that share the introduced dependency.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName in~ ("package.json",".npmrc")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","code.exe","Code.exe","devenv.exe","git.exe","notepad.exe","notepad++.exe","explorer.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","cursor.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("package.json",".npmrc")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","code.exe","devenv.exe","git.exe","notepad.exe","notepad++.exe","explorer.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","cursor.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

detection:

  filter_legit:

level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\package.json OR *\\.npmrc) -@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\code.exe OR *\\devenv.exe OR *\\git.exe OR *\\notepad.exe OR *\\notepad++.exe OR *\\explorer.exe OR *\\WindowsTerminal.exe OR *\\cursor.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\(package\.json|\.npmrc)$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(npm|yarn|node|pnpm|code|devenv|git|notepad|notepad\+\+|explorer|WindowsTerminal|cursor)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name IN ("package.json",".npmrc")) AND (Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")) AND NOT (Filesystem.process_name IN ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","code.exe","devenv.exe","git.exe","notepad.exe","notepad++.exe","explorer.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","cursor.exe")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name IN ("package.json",".npmrc")) AND (Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")) AND NOT (Filesystem.process_name IN ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","code.exe","devenv.exe","git.exe","notepad.exe","notepad++.exe","explorer.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","cursor.exe")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
node-gyp native module rebuild spawning unexpected compiler chain AIInstallation Low
Hunts the implicit binding.gyp build path the article calls out explicitly: 'a package with a binding.gyp and no explicit install script still gets blocked, because npm runs an implicit node-gyp rebuild for it'. Surfaces npm/node spawning compiler or interpreter tooling (cl.exe, msbuild.exe, python.exe, powershell.exe, cmd.exe) via node-gyp / rebuild so analysts can spot a backdoored native module addition that bypasses the obvious lifecycle-hook signal. Rationale: Article explicitly names binding.gyp + implicit node-gyp rebuild as a default-deny target — a clear article-anchored hunt for the compiler/interpreter chain a malicious native module would invoke. Tier=hunting + confidence=Low because legitimate native modules (sqlite3, bcrypt, sharp, node-sass) emit the same chain; the hunt is for rare/first-seen package contexts.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • legitimate native module install: sqlite3, bcrypt, node-sass, sharp, canvas
  • electron-rebuild after Electron version bump
  • node-pre-gyp prebuilt-binary download falling back to source build
  • developer first-time installing native module on fresh laptop with VS Build Tools
  • CI pipeline installing native deps in a Docker build stage
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\sqlite3\",@"\node_modules\bcrypt\",@"\node_modules\sharp\",@"\node_modules\node-sass\",@"\node_modules\canvas\",@"\node_modules\@parcel\watcher\"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify which package's binding.gyp triggered the build (walk InitiatingProcessFolderPath under node_modules) and check it against your package allowlist / popularity baseline. Hash the resulting .node file. Step 2 (contain): if the package is unknown or recently published, isolate the host, block the package@version in the internal registry, and roll back node_modules from lockfile. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the package name to find other hosts that installed it in the same window; check git history of the project that pulled it for the dependency-add commit; submit the compiled .node and SHA256 to malware analysis.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","node-gyp.exe","node-gyp.cmd")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","binding.gyp","rebuild","configure")
| where FileName in~ ("cl.exe","link.exe","msbuild.exe","python.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","gcc.exe","g++.exe","make.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","node-gyp.exe","node-gyp.cmd")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","binding.gyp","rebuild","configure")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cl.exe","link.exe","msbuild.exe","python.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","gcc.exe","g++.exe","make.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: node-gyp Rebuild Spawning Compiler or Script Engine
id: d7f2a4b5-ae6c-4d9f-cf4a-5b1d8c0e3f4a
description: Detects node-gyp rebuild chains where npm/node spawns compiler or interpreter tooling (cl.exe, msbuild.exe, python.exe, powershell.exe) — the implicit binding.gyp build path GitHub flagged as a default-deny target in npm v12.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\node-gyp.exe'
      - '\node-gyp.cmd'
  selection_gyp:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'node-gyp'
      - 'binding.gyp'
      - 'rebuild'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cl.exe'
      - '\link.exe'
      - '\msbuild.exe'
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\gcc.exe'
      - '\make.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
level: low
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentCommandLine:(*node-gyp* OR *binding.gyp* OR *rebuild*) OR @CommandLine:(*node-gyp* OR *binding.gyp*)) @ParentImage:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\node-gyp.exe) @Image:(*\\cl.exe OR *\\link.exe OR *\\msbuild.exe OR *\\MSBuild.exe OR *\\python.exe OR *\\Python.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\gcc.exe OR *\\make.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(npm|yarn|node|pnpm|node-gyp)\.(exe|cmd)$/i
| regex("(?i)(node-gyp|binding\\.gyp|rebuild|configure)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| ImageFileName=/\\(cl|link|msbuild|python|powershell|pwsh|cmd|gcc|g\+\+|make)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","node-gyp.exe","node-gyp.cmd")) AND (Processes.parent_process IN ("*node-gyp*","*binding.gyp*","*rebuild*","*configure*")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("cl.exe","link.exe","msbuild.exe","python.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","gcc.exe","g++.exe","make.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","yarn.exe","node.exe","pnpm.exe","node-gyp.exe","node-gyp.cmd")) AND (Processes.parent_process IN ("*node-gyp*","*binding.gyp*","*rebuild*","*configure*")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("cl.exe","link.exe","msbuild.exe","python.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","gcc.exe","g++.exe","make.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |

    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic

references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:

        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:

level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",

| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`

    where Authentication.action="success"

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-10520 — Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-06-11 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution. This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors. Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.

Baileys exploit signal — messages.upsert with requestId / placeholderResendMessa AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact exploit primitive from CVE-2026-48063: a Baileys session receives a placeholderResendMessage triggering a fake messages.upsert event carrying a requestId field. The vendor workaround literally tells operators to drop messages.upsert events that contain a requestId — so any application log emitting both strings in proximity is either an active exploit attempt or pre-patch traffic that needs filtering. Rationale: Article workaround text explicitly identifies `messages.upsert` events carrying a `requestId` field as the exploit primitive driven by `placeholderResendMessage` — three article-specific tokens used in a single proximity match keeps FP rate very low. Cross-checked GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg patch commit 3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35 to confirm the field names emerge from the protocolMessage handler. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/commit/3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35 • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48063
ATT&CKT1190 T1565.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer reproducing the issue locally with the patched test harness
  • Security research/red-team logs from internal exploit validation
  • Pre-patch debug logs already capturing requestId for unrelated message resend traces
  • Documentation/comment blocks containing the literal strings being echoed by hot-reload loggers
Suppression filter
| where not (SyslogMessage has_any ("test_placeholderResend","jest","__test__","integration-test"))
Response runbook
Triage: confirm Baileys version on the alerting host via `npm ls baileys`/`npm ls @whiskeysockets/baileys`; if < 6.7.22 or in the 7.0.0-rc1..rc12 range, treat as live exploit. Pull the raw message body and check whether the message key/JID matches a known internal sender. Contain: pause the Baileys process, rotate the WhatsApp pairing/session, and apply the `shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false` workaround plus the `requestId` filter until upgrade. Hunt: pivot on the same host for unsolicited history sync events, fake app-state-sync key shares, and any messages persisted into the application DB whose sender JID disagrees with the signing key.

| where ActionType == "ProcessCreated" or ActionType startswith "AppControl" or ActionType == "AntimalwareEngineLoaded" or isnotempty(AdditionalFields)
| where AdditionalFields has "placeholderResendMessage" and AdditionalFields has "messages.upsert"
| where AdditionalFields has "requestId"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog

| where ProcessName has_any ("node","nodejs","pm2","baileys")

| where SyslogMessage has "messages.upsert"
| where SyslogMessage has "requestId"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Baileys package.json dropped into node_modules AIWeaponization Medium
Inventory pivot: surface hosts where a vulnerable @whiskeysockets/baileys or baileys package lands on disk via npm install, container image extraction, or git clone. Targets the article's affected version ranges so SOC can drive patch compliance. Rationale: Article specifies the affected npm packages by exact name: `npm:baileys` and `npm:@whiskeysockets/baileys`. The package.json file inside the package directory is the deterministic install fingerprint regardless of pnpm/yarn/npm or container layer extraction. This is hunt-tier because it doesn't read the version field — UC7 covers the version cut. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg • https://www.npmjs.com/package/baileys
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI/CD build agents running `npm install` for projects that pin patched versions — benign
  • Developer workstations cloning sample WhatsApp bots from GitHub
  • Docker layer cache extraction in a build farm refreshing the same image dozens of times
  • Security researcher's analysis sandbox unpacking vendored copies
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("build-agent","runner-","ci-") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe"))
Response runbook
Triage: open the package.json that was written and read the `version` field — anything < 6.7.22 or in 7.0.0-rc.1..7.0.0-rc11 is vulnerable. Map the host to its function (dev vs. production chatbot vs. container host). Contain: if production, drive an immediate `npm install baileys@latest` or `npm install @whiskeysockets/baileys@7.0.0-rc12` and redeploy the service. Hunt: query all hosts in the org with this file written in the last 30 days and intersect with the running-process telemetry from UC3 to find live vulnerable instances vs. dormant copies.

| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Writers=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 5) by DeviceName, FolderPath
| order by LastSeen desc

Node.js process loading Baileys at runtime AIInstallation Medium
Detects Node.js (or pm2/forever/nodemon-wrapped Node) processes whose command line or working directory points at the Baileys library — the runtime fingerprint of an exploitable session. Rationale: Pairs the article's named packages with the only runtime that loads them (Node.js / its wrappers). The cmdline `has_any ("baileys","@whiskeysockets/baileys")` is the live-process equivalent of UC2's file-write detection, and together they let analysts separate dormant clones from genuinely exploitable services. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg
ATT&CKT1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running `node test-baileys.js` in a sandbox on a workstation
  • CI test runner instantiating the library to run unit tests against a mocked socket
  • Container build smoke-tests invoking the library briefly before image bake
  • Internal helpdesk bot already running on a patched version (UC7 needs to dedupe)
Response runbook
Triage: pull the working directory and resolve the package.json under it to read the actual installed version. Cross-reference against UC2/UC7 inventory. Contain: if production and vulnerable, drain the process, upgrade with `npm install baileys@7.0.0-rc12` or `baileys@6.7.22`, and redeploy. Hunt: enumerate every Node.js host running Baileys, build a per-tenant inventory, and ensure UC1/UC4/UC5 telemetry forwarders are in place before the exploit detection rules can be effective.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe","node","pm2","nodemon.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("baileys","@whiskeysockets/baileys")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Cmds=make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 3) by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate

| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(\\|/)(node(\.exe)?|pm2|nodemon(\.exe)?)$"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("baileys","@whiskeysockets/baileys")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Cmds=make_set(ActingProcessCommandLine, 3) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| order by LastSeen desc

Spoofed messages.upsert — sender / key signature mismatch in Baileys app log AIActions on Objectives Medium
Impact-phase detection: catches the article's downstream effect (spoofed messages.upsert with fake message key + payload) by parsing Baileys application logs for validation failures, signature mismatches, or sender-key disagreements emitted by the patched validation code. Rationale: Article body identifies the impact as a `messages.upsert` event carrying a fake message key + payload. Validation failures emitted by the patched code (and existing signal/libsignal callers) are the cleanest impact-phase fingerprint. Searching for the literal `messages.upsert` token alongside cryptographic-validation failure strings keeps the rule article-specific. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg • https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/commit/3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35
ATT&CKT1565.002 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine key rotation by a remote party causing transient `sender-key-distribution` warnings during catch-up
  • WhatsApp Web protocol upgrades changing identity-key format causing parser noise
  • Group membership churn producing legitimate `invalid sender key` lines until the SKDM re-shares
  • Developer testing message validation locally with intentionally bad payloads
Suppression filter
| where not (SyslogMessage has_any ("sender-key-distribution-message","SenderKeyDistributionMessage") and not SyslogMessage has "unverified sender")
Response runbook
Triage: extract the JID from the log line and confirm it's a legitimate counterparty for this Baileys tenant (CRM lookup or chat-history audit). Pull the surrounding 2 minutes of log lines to see whether `placeholderResendMessage` fired immediately before. Contain: quarantine the message in the application DB (do not surface to end-user / downstream automation), force a re-pair of the WhatsApp session, and rotate the noise-handshake key. Hunt: correlate JID across other Baileys hosts in the fleet — if the same JID is triggering signature mismatches across multiple tenants, the attacker is sweeping. Also pivot to UC1 for the upstream `requestId` indicator.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AdditionalFields has "messages.upsert"
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("signature mismatch","invalid sender key","sender-key-distribution","unverified sender","identity key mismatch","jid mismatch")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has_any ("node","nodejs","pm2","baileys")
| where SyslogMessage has "messages.upsert"
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("signature mismatch","invalid sender key","sender-key-distribution","unverified sender","identity key mismatch","jid mismatch")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:linux.syslog OR source:nodejs OR source:kubernetes) @process.name:(*node* OR *baileys* OR *pm2*) "messages.upsert" ("signature mismatch" OR "invalid sender key" OR "sender-key-distribution" OR "unverified sender" OR "identity key mismatch" OR "jid mismatch")
CLOUD
search index=* sourcetype IN ("baileys","nodejs:app","docker:container","kubernetes:container") "messages.upsert" ("signature mismatch" OR "invalid sender key" OR "sender-key-distribution" OR "verifyMessage" OR "unverified sender" OR "identity key mismatch" OR "jid mismatch") | rex field=_raw "(?<jid>\d{6,}@s\.whatsapp\.net|\d{6,}@g\.us)" | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(jid) as jids by host | where count >= 1 | sort - count
Baileys app-state-sync corruption — rollback / version conflict bursts AIActions on Objectives Medium
Targets the article's second impact vector: corrupting the app-state-sync system via fake key shares. Surfaces hosts where Baileys logs rapid app-state rollbacks, hash mismatches, or version conflicts following a protocolMessage processing error — the in-the-wild signature of the appStateSyncKeyShare jamming primitive. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out the attacker can `corrupt the app state sync system by sending fake key shares` and notes there is no workaround for app-state-sync jamming, so this is one of the highest-value detection targets. The 5-minute burst threshold separates a one-off retry from sustained jamming. Source strings (`appStateSync`, `AppStateSyncKeyShare`) match the Baileys repo function names. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg • https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys
ATT&CKT1565.002 T1499.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine SKDM resync after a network partition heals
  • Multi-device pairing churn from end-users adding/removing companion devices
  • Baileys process restart causing one-off resync attempts
  • DB corruption from a non-attack cause (disk full, OOM) producing the same error class
Response runbook
Triage: pull the 5-minute window of log lines and look for an upstream `placeholderResendMessage` or unexpected `protocolMessage` parse log right before the burst started. Confirm Baileys version is in the vulnerable range. Contain: if vulnerable, upgrade and restart with a fresh state DB — the corrupted state may not be recoverable in-place per the advisory. Hunt: check whether the same source JID appears in UC4's mismatch logs in the same window; pivot to UC1's `requestId` signal to identify the originating exploit message.

| summarize EventCount=count(), Samples=make_set(AdditionalFields, 3) by bin(Timestamp, 5m), DeviceName
| where EventCount > 3
| order by Timestamp desc

| summarize EventCount=count(), Samples=make_set(SyslogMessage, 3) by bin(TimeGenerated, 5m), Computer
